Q: How Claude can get access to GitLab/Github issues? A:

Note none of the response is AI generated or augmented. This response is created fully by a human with their own squishy mind.

Overview

The assumption is you want there to be a local copy of the issues in some sort of issue-number_project_site.md files.

For example if you have 2 issues in Project A on Github. You'd expect to see 1_A_Github.md and 2_A_Github.md

Same logic for Gitlab. If you had 2 issues in Project B on Gitlab. You'd expect to see 1_B_Gitlab.md' and 2_B_Gitlab.md`

What I'm not answering as it's not stated nor is there one way to do it would be syncing local modifications of changes to *.md files back to respective GitHub and GitLab issue trackers.

Suggested Steps

I've done this with Claude, if you're on a paid plan. You'll want to build two skills.

The first skill would pull issue from GitHub. You can either build the script manually or get Claude's assistence with it. When I was using Claude, it was able to figure it out pretty quickly. However if you prefer manual approach, GitHub's API documentation

The simplest is if you're traversing several projects, hard coding is probably quicker then auto discover. Then from each project in GitHub you'll be able to enumerate the issues and dump them into a pretty local markdown.

Same for GitLab, however heads up, you may need to generate an API key per project? But I hope my information for that is out of date and you can use a single API key to iterate all your projects and related issues from that. GitLab Rest API documentation

Finally you should now have the files in the directory.

Q: getting 'internet not reachable' with sdkman A:

Use OSX curl:

/usr/bin/curl -vvv https://api.sdkman.io/2

If this work, then you are using a problematic curl version like macports; uninstall or upgrade you macports version or remove macports if you aren't using this.
